title: Man justifying himself: asserting innocence
source_text: III. Eodem sensu sumitur verbum justificandi, ubi dicitur homo seipsum justificare, quando vel suam innocentiam asserit, vel suam justitiam vendicat. Ut quum apud Lucam, cap. 10. Legisperitus quidam volens justificare seipsum, dixit ad Jesum, Quis est proximus meus. Et quum in eodem libro, cap. 16. sic increpat Christus Pharisaeos, Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus, Deus autem novit corda vestra.
pass_a_gloss: In the same sense the verb of justifying is taken when a man is said to justify himself, when either he asserts his innocence or claims his righteousness. As when in Luke 10 a certain lawyer, wishing to justify himself, said to Jesus, Who is my neighbor? And when in the same book, chapter 16, Christ thus rebukes the Pharisees: You are they who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts.
pass_b_english: Same forensic sense when a man justifies himself—asserts innocence or claims righteousness.
Lk 10 lawyer; Lk 16 Pharisees who justify themselves before men.
